question: In which Union Territory is the 'slash and burn' agriculture known as 'Dipa'?

options.text: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dipa** is the term used for 'slash and burn' agriculture in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
• 'Slash and burn' agriculture, also known as shifting cultivation, involves clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning the vegetation, and then using the cleared land for farming.
 
• This agricultural practice is commonly seen among tribal communities in various regions, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The practice is traditionally followed by indigenous communities to cultivate crops for a few years until the soil fertility diminishes, after which they move to a new area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are a group of islands at the southeastern edge of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The islands are home to several indigenous tribes, each with unique cultural practices and traditional agricultural methods.
 
• Shifting cultivation is a sustainable practice when done on a small scale and with sufficient fallow periods for the land to recover.
 
• However, large-scale and frequent shifting cultivation can lead to deforestation and soil degradation.
